text:
Jon: hey everyone, day 1 at Redwood! MacBook Air M2. Quickboot problems: asdf not loading node, and my ssh keys keep asking for passphrase every git push. Any quick pointers?
Priya: welcome! :wave: first check Xcode CLT + Homebrew for arm64. Is brew in /opt/homebrew? run `which brew`.
Jon: brew is /opt/homebrew yes. I installed asdf with brew and added `source /opt/homebrew/opt/asdf/libexec/asdf.sh` to ~/.zshrc like the guide. `asdf list` gives errors.
Maya: if `asdf` commands are not found, try `eval "$(asdf init -)"` in your shell init (zprofile/zshrc order matters). Put PATH changes in ~/.zprofile so GUI apps pick them up.
Jon: tried that. Now `asdf plugin-add nodejs` fails: gpg key import error.
Priya: nodejs plugin requires fetching Node.js release keys. Install gpg via brew `brew install gpg` and run `bash ~/.asdf/plugins/nodejs/bin/import-release-team-keyring`.
Jon: ok that worked, installed node 18. But VS Code terminal still shows node v20. `which node` points to /usr/local/bin/node.
Maya: you probably had an intel brew leftover. Make sure /opt/homebrew/bin is earlier in PATH. Check `echo $PATH` and update ~/.zprofile to prepend /opt/homebrew/bin then `exec $SHELL`.
Jon: PATH fixed, node v18 now. SSH issue: `ssh-add -l` shows "Could not open a connection to your authentication agent." I use 1Password for SSH.
Priya: for mac, add these lines to ~/.ssh/config: `AddKeysToAgent yes`, `UseKeychain yes`, and `IdentityFile ~/.ssh/id_ed25519`. Also use `ssh-add --apple-use-keychain ~/.ssh/id_ed25519` to store it.
Maya: watch out for spawning ssh-agent in project .envrc files! If direnv runs its own agent you'll get multiple agents and keys not forwarded. Remove agent starts from .envrc.
Jon: omg i did have `eval "$(ssh-agent -s)"` in a project .envrc. removing it fixed prompts. thanks.
Priya: one more tip: if you use devcontainers, add "remoteEnv": { "PATH": "/opt/homebrew/bin:${containerEnv:PATH}" } in devcontainer.json so tools resolve inside container.
Jon: brilliant. everything green now 389 thanks team.
DevEx Bot: Congrats Jon! If you want, run `curl -fsSL https://get.redwood.dev/bootstrap | bash` to auto-install recommended tools. Docs: https://intranet.redwood/company/onboarding/dev-setup. Ping #devex for walkthroughs.
